correctness.rationale: For arbitrary nonzero real sup-norm vectors, directional derivatives yield the exact sign-straddling Birkhoff–James criterion. Zeroing non-active coordinates can only move entries to zero and preserves the criterion in each direction; mutually orthogonal projective vertices never collapse under rounding. Ternary mutual adjacency is precisely signed-support incomparability. Uniform maximal chains of signed subsets prove the LYM inequality sum 1/[binom(n,k)2^(k-1)] ≤ 1 for antichains, yielding the universal upper bound, while the complete maximizing rank provides equality. The reasoning includes n=1 and all n, without finite-to-infinite inference. The standalone checker independently performs finite combinatorial diagnostic tests (74,190 ternary pairs, 15,628 preserved grid edges).

originality.rationale: The closest published 2026 result states the same binomial expression only as a lower bound and expressly leaves a matching upper bound unproved. The 2021 original gives only a smaller full-support lower construction and a non-sharp general upper, while the 2024 open-access norm-recognition article does not specify this clique number. The new proof gives a clique-preserving active-coordinate rounding from unrestricted real vectors to an antipodal signed-subset poset, then a matching signed LYM upper bound. Public and published-finding corpus searches found no stronger covering theorem; residual risks are stated.

value.rationale: The clique number of the mutual Birkhoff–James orthograph is an established natural geometric graph invariant; its supremum-norm value was previously bounded below by a large explicitly constructed signed support layer but was not determined in the inspected direct predecessor. The exact classification for all dimensions gives a matching universal upper bound, turns an infinite-vertex optimization into a finite Sperner-width problem, and identifies where the largest cliques occur. This is an exact motivated invariant, not an arbitrary slice or an unmotivated finite enumeration.
